transcript.text: Bosch KGN34NL3AG - some days it's fine, other days it just clicks every few minutes at the back and doesn't seem to run, and the freezer starts getting soft. Then it starts working again by itself. What's going on?

That clicking sound followed by no cooling usually means the compressor is trying to start but tripping its internal safety switch before it can run. The most common cause is a failed start relay (a small plastic component on the side of the compressor), though the compressor itself could be overheating or failing. To rule out simple issues, please check that the plug is fully inserted and the socket has power, and ensure the cooling coils at the back or underneath aren't clogged with dust or pushed tight against the wall.

Thank you. It is plugged directly into the wall socket and I tried another socket with the same result, so it isn't the socket. The back is a bit dusty but there is a gap behind it. The compressor also feels very hot to touch when it's clicking, and there's no burning smell and nothing trips.

The symptoms—specifically the rapid clicking with no start, combined with the compressor getting very hot—are classic signs of a failed start relay or overload protector. This small component sits on the side of the compressor; when it fails, it cuts power to prevent the compressor from burning out, causing that click-cycle. The next step is to visually inspect this part. Please unplug the fridge, remove the rear lower panel to expose the compressor, and check if the small black plastic box (the relay) attached to it looks burnt, melted, or feels loose/cracked. Let me know what you see.

Thank you. I can pull the fridge out and take the lower rear panel off, but I'd like to know what I'm looking for first. I'm not sure what the relay looks like, so could you describe it and tell me anything I should be careful of? I have a basic multimeter but I'm not confident using it.

The start relay is a small black plastic block, roughly the size of a large matchbox, clipped directly onto the metal casing of the compressor. It usually has three flat metal pins sticking out that plug into the compressor terminals, and two wires leading away from it to the fridge's mains supply. Be very careful: only touch the plastic housing, never the metal pins or the compressor body itself while it is hot, and ensure the appliance remains unplugged. If you see any scorch marks, melting, or if the box feels loose or cracked on the casing, that suggests the relay has failed.

Thank you, that is clear. I'll unplug it, pull it out and take the lower rear panel off, then have a look at the relay and tell you what I see. Should I do anything else while it's open, or just look at the relay?

Just have a good visual and tactile look at the relay itself for now. Check if the black plastic box feels loose or wobbly on the compressor casing, and look closely to see if there are any signs of burning, melting, or cracking on the plastic. If it looks damaged or feels loose, that suggests the relay has failed and needs replacing. If it looks perfectly solid and clean, we will need to consider whether the compressor itself is seizing up.
Thank you, I'll do that and report back on what the relay looks like. Is there anything I should be careful of when pulling the fridge out, apart from keeping it unplugged?

When pulling the fridge out, ensure you have a clear path and use a sturdy surface (like a piece of cardboard) to protect the floor. Be careful not to kink or crush the cooling coils at the back; if they are copper pipes, handle them gently as they can bend easily. Once it is out, keep it upright to avoid damaging the compressor oil, and just give that relay a visual check for now.
Thank you, that is helpful. I'll go ahead, keep it unplugged and upright, and report back on what the relay looks like once I've had a look.

Please take your time with that. Once you've had a good look, just let me know if the black plastic box felt loose or wobbly on the compressor casing, and whether there were any signs of burning, melting, or cracking on the plastic itself.

I haven't managed to look at it yet, so I can't tell you whether it's loose, burnt or cracked. If it looks fine, or I can't tell, what would you want me to do next? I'd be willing to pay up to about £150 for a repair, as I value the fridge.

If the relay looks fine (no burns, cracks, or looseness), the next step is to check if the compressor itself is mechanically seized. With the fridge unplugged and the rear panel off, you can try gently turning the compressor shaft (usually accessible via a central bolt or pulley on top of the motor) by hand; if it won't budge at all, the compressor is likely seized. Please go ahead with the visual inspection and tell me exactly what you see on that black plastic box.
